nodes.name: Kessler Reservoir pipeline
nodes.summary: The Kessler Reservoir pipeline was built in 1961. HVWA chief executive Tomas Reyes announced a plan in January to replace it by raising household water tariffs by 18 percent. Mayor Ilse Varga called the pipeline "a failure waiting to happen".

nodes.name: city council
nodes.summary: The Harbor Vale city council received a statement from Mayor Ilse Varga supporting an 18 percent household water tariff increase to replace the 1961 Kessler Reservoir pipeline. Council member Daniel Oyelaran, who chairs the finance committee, opposed the rise, arguing low-income households would bear the burden. After the Harbor Vale Courier exposed a conflict of interest involving HVWA chief executive Tomas Reyes and his brother, Oyelaran requested state auditor Grace Lindqvist to examine the Brightline Consulting contract. Lindqvist opened a formal audit in March. On 2 April, Mayor Varga withdrew support for the tariff increase, calling for a pause to rebuild public trust. In June, the audit found the Brightline contract broke procurement rules but found no evidence Tomas Reyes personally profited. The council is scheduled to vote on a revised 9 percent tariff plan on 15 July. Daniel Oyelaran now supports the revised plan.
